messages.author: fe0b9140b8bdf3c1
messages.subject: segfault with ggplot2 parameter
parts:
Hi Rapache folks -

I've got this strange error where RApache segfaults on this one line
in my code.

Yet running it on the server terminal CLI yields a fine result,
without a crash.

The offending line isn't much -- just an operation in ggplot2 to fill
polygons with a given color.

library(ggplot2)
library(maps)
p <- qplot(long,
lat,
data = df,
fill = volume, ## <-- this line causes RApache to
segfault
group=group,
geom = "polygon")

The file is running at http://dashr.metamarketsgroup.com/plotState

This is the graphic it should be showing:

http://dashr.metamarketsgroup.com/images/file79838cb2.png

Here's the relevant line from the Apache error logs:

[Sat Jan 23 12:13:59 2010] [notice] child pid 19302 exit signal
Segmentation fault (11)

MD

--
Michael Driscoll : Metamarkets
350 Townsend #270: SF 94107
415-860-4347

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: segfault with ggplot2 parameter
parts:
Usually when I see seg faults in the server logs it's due to R being
updated (from a binary release with apt-get) while rapache is not. You
can get away with this for awhile, but then strange things happen like
weird errors messages and seg faults. Re-installing rapache fixes it.

Jeff

I've re-installed Rapache on one machine, and did a fresh install on a second.

The error is reproducible on both machines, running two different
flavors of Ubuntu 8.10, both with R 2.10.1.

device. Running these as www-data on the machines works just fine.

activity=c(1,2,3))
p <- qplot(x, y, data = df) ## works

messages.author: fe0b9140b8bdf3c1
messages.subject: Re: segfault with ggplot2 parameter
parts:
Thanks Jeroen. I resolved it by moving to a newer Ubuntu distro.

The current set up that is working is:

Ubuntu 9.04 (jaunty), Apache 2.2.11-2, RApache 1.1.8, R 2.10.1, ggplot2_0.8.5

In case anyone comes across errors like this in the future, the two
set-ups that reproducibly yielded these seg faults were

Ubuntu 8.04 (hardy), Apache 2.2.8-1, RApache 1.1.8, R 2.10.1, ggplot2_0.8.5
Ubuntu 8.10 (intrepid), Apache 2.2.9-7, RApache 1.1.8, R 2.10.1,
ggplot2_0.8.5

MD

postscripts:
1. R's "sessionInfo()" function describes versions of packages loaded
in your current environment
2. On Ubuntu command line, "lsb_release -a" & "apt-cache policy
apache2" yield release & Apache versions

Those are good to know.

Another issue that could cause seg faults is C code in packages that
were compiled against older R versions. Using update.packages
(ask=FALSE) or something similar after you upgrade R is a good idea.
Problems though do arise if you use a mix of installed packages via
apt-get and install.packages().

Jeff
